Thanks for the call this morning. We chatted internally and have one more ask on the pricing exhibit: we need the step-up (commit increase) trigger to include a temporary forgiveness window in the first 180 days after go-live for volume anomalies tied to onboarding (we've seen major spikes in ingest costs during pilot). Can Redwood propose concrete language for that? Also want to confirm what the recovery lifecycle looks like if usage drops again (we're trying to avoid immediate clawbacks).

Subject: RE: Step-up commit trigger & recovery lifecycle — pricing exhibit redlines

Sofia / Jordan / team —

Thanks for the context, Jordan. I reviewed the matrix and drafted redline language for the Pricing Exhibit and an operational appendix. Key points of the proposed redline (high level):

1) Forgiveness Window (onboarding): For the first 180 days following Go-Live, a Step-Up Trigger will only be enforced where the 30-day rolling average utilization exceeds the Step-Up Threshold for at least 90 of any 120 consecutive calendar days. This creates the requested buffer for onboarding spikes.

2) Recovery Lifecycle (grace and phased recovery): If utilization subsequently declines below the Step-Up Threshold, the parties will follow a 3-stage recovery lifecycle: a 60-day observation period (no retroactive true-up), then a 90-day phased true-up where incremental crediting is applied at 50% of the delta in months 1–3, and 100% thereafter, capped to the amount collected under the Step-Up during the prior 12 months. This limits clawback exposure while protecting revenue.

3) Credit mechanics: Credits will be applied as invoice line-item adjustments (not cash refunds) unless otherwise requested in writing; credits expire after 12 months. True-ups will appear on the first invoice following the end of each recovery phase.

4) Audit & disputes: Redwood will provide usage reports and a 30-day dispute window following any true-up. Disputes that remain unresolved after 30 days escalate to bilateral arbitration per Section 12 of the Master Agreement.

5) Definitions and examples: I added a short example table to the appendix illustrating the phased recovery math and capped-clawback logic (see attached redline PDF).

Open items for Sales ops to confirm: whether credits need to be proforma-able in our billing system as negative invoice lines (Marissa), and whether Finance prefers a cap aggregation at the customer account level vs. per-order form line item (Karthik).

I attach a clean annotated PDF with the redlines and the step_up_recovery_matrix.csv from Acme with our notes. If this aligns, I'll request Legal sign-off and ask Contracts to fold the language into the final Order Form.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
